name: Iron a dress shirt
blurb: An order of operations that takes about five minutes and gives a genuinely crisp result — collar, cuffs, sleeves, yoke, then the body.
gear: An iron with a steam function
steps: Check the care label and set the correct temperature. Start cooler than you think; you can always go hotter.
Iron slightly damp, or use steam — dry ironing sets creases rather than removing them.
Do the collar first: underside then top, working from the points inwards to avoid pushing creases into the tips.
Do the cuffs next, unbuttoned and flat, inside then out.
Do the sleeves, aligning the seam and pressing from the shoulder down. Decide deliberately whether you want a crease in the sleeve.
Do the yoke across the shoulders, then the two front panels and the back, and hang it immediately on a hanger.
tips: Ironing over buttons breaks them. Work around and between.
Hang it straight away. Folding a warm shirt reintroduces every crease you just removed.
Work small sections at a time rather than dragging the iron across the whole shirt.
proof: A shirt with a crisp collar, flat cuffs and no double creases, done in about five minutes.
